judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":302,"endChar":441,"text":"libertarian free will doesn't matter at all because having it wouldn't give you responsibility not having it wouldn't take it away from you"}}
judgments.rationale: The clause says libertarian free will is the wrong governing demand because possessing or lacking it would not alter responsibility.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":73,"endChar":170,"text":"we want to know about responsibility and whether whether we deserve blame and praise and so forth"}}
judgments.rationale: The response expressly substitutes the question whether people deserve blame and praise, making responsibility the governing demand.
The response explicitly identifies the original framing's defect as a confusion between causation and control.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":132,"endChar":209,"text":"you haven't told us what their upbringing was how much self-control they have"}}
judgments.rationale: It replaces causal-history sufficiency with an express demand for facts about upbringing and, decisively, how much self-control the agents have.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":46,"endChar":295,"text":"the more philosophically relevant question is not whether or not those practices would be justified but the question about whether certain types of reactive attitudes would be justified because those are the ones that are philosophically significant"}}
judgments.rationale: The comparative clause rejects justification of practices as the philosophically relevant framing and explains that reactive attitudes are the significant issue.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":150,"endChar":231,"text":"the question about whether certain types of reactive attitudes would be justified"}}
judgments.rationale: The response expressly installs whether specified reactive attitudes are justified as the replacement governing question.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":115,"endChar":390,"text":"the question is whether or not those distinctions are enough to ground the kinds of more dessert-based moral practices that we're debating um and i do think those those those distinctions matter they matter in all kinds of important ways but they matter for different reasons"}}
judgments.rationale: The response explains that the compatibilist distinctions can matter for important but different reasons, so their mere importance is malformed as a desert-grounding test.

judgments.resolvedJson: {"value":true,"evidence":{"startChar":115,"endChar":253,"text":"the question is whether or not those distinctions are enough to ground the kinds of more dessert-based moral practices that we're debating"}}
